content.text:
I've re-engineered the `components` (plain HTML) scaffold in `packages/scaffold/templates/components/`.

**What changed and why:**

The old scaffold put a giant markup string inside `src/main.ts` and injected it with `innerHTML`. That's the anti-pattern you flagged: no view-source content, a flash of an empty page, worse accessibility/SEO, and it forces every future edit to happen inside a JS template literal instead of real HTML.

The modern, dev-friendly shape for a plain HTML/CSS/TS(Vite) app is the same one Vite's own vanilla-ts template and the rest of pantoken's own framework scaffolds (Vue, Angular, Svelte) already use — markup lives where its language is native, and JS is reserved for behavior:

- [templates/components/index.html](packages/scaffold/templates/components/index.html) now contains the actual page shell (the same `@pantoken/plugin-layouts` "wrapper" markup, generated the identical way Vue/Angular/Svelte templates already do it) — no `#app` div, no injection.
- [templates/components/src/main.ts.tmpl](packages/scaffold/templates/components/src/main.ts.tmpl) is now just the pantoken CSS/interactions imports plus a comment marking where to add interactive JS/TS.
- Added `src/style.css` for the user's own app-specific styles, imported from `main.ts` (the standard Vite convention).
- Updated the template's README to describe the new file responsibilities.

I regenerated `generated/scaffolds.ts` (`vp run generate`) and confirmed with a fresh scaffold to a temp dir plus the `@pantoken/scaffold` and `create-pantoken-app` test suites (all passing, 84 + 8 tests). Added a changeset for the user-visible change.

This only touches the template source in this repo — `test1/` is a generated artifact and isn't something to hand-edit; regenerating it (`npx create-pantoken-app` → `components`) once this ships will produce the new structure.
